transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi there, I'm Dora, a clinical conversational agent. I can help answer your questions about cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hello, yes, I do have some questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise, such as gardening, one week after surgery. However, you should avoid strenuous exercise for a month. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. However, if you have significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after your operation. This should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all I needed to know. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! So, just to confirm, all your questions have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thanks again for your assistance!

verdict.label: pass
